content:
Would I have passed my G2 if I didn't make my instant-fail mistake?
Why I failed/short vent

I'm really disappointed in myself for doing what I did during the test. I was caught by surprise when the examiner asked me to take a different route (my instructor previously assured me they only used route 2 in Etobicoke) at an intersection. He asked to make a left turn and I was afraid I was turning too slow so I was about to start moving as oncoming cars appeared far away and there was a bus stopped but he slammed the break on the other side. I felt so bad at this point and I just wanted to break down and start apologising on the spot but he continued the test. I can't believe my test anxiety got to me like this because I KNOW to wait until it's clear on the opposite side. Even my instructor was surprised that was the big mistake I made because he knew that wasn't how I drove. The next mistake I made was not emphasising my blindspot checks enough/fully turning my body to look at the left side. I'll try to turn my shoulders more as well next time.  

  
What's next for me

Sept is fully booked so now I'm planning on taking 3 lessons and retaking the test with my instructor's car in early October. I see that I have also been deducted points for driving slow which is understandable since I sometimes dropped 3-5 under the speed limit on a road that I assumed was 50km/h (no signage) while listening to the examiner's instructions. I'll definitely work on that since multitasking is a skill I'll need for future driving too. Aside from my initial question, is there anything I missed that I should try to work on?

  
Thank you
